title: Encoded PowerShell attack on WORKSTATION6 disabling security controls
summary: An encoded PowerShell command ran as SYSTEM on WORKSTATION6 via cmd.exe, decoded to reveal commands disabling script block logging and AMSI, then downloading and executing code from external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious, outside company network ranges). The attack chain includes T1059.001 powerShell execution, T1027 obfuscation, T1105 ingress tool transfer, and T1562.001 defense evasion.
evidence: Encoded PowerShell command (-enc flag) launched by cmd.exe as parent process on WORKSTATION6

Decoded command shows: disables_script_block_logging=true, bypasses_amsi_antivirus_scan=true, downloads_from_web=true, runs_downloaded_code=true, contains_nested_base64=true, uses_proxy_credentials=true
Command contacts IP 10.10.10.5 which is flagged as suspicious - private address not in company's known network ranges
Process chain: services.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (with -enc) -> conhost.exe
Follow-on processes include WmiPrvSE.exe (NETWORK SERVICE) and whoami.exe (SYSTEM)
MITRE techniques confirmed: T1059.001 PowerShell execution, T1027 obfuscated files/information, T1105 ingress tool transfer, T1562.001 impair defenses

recommended_actions.action: Block communication with IP 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy level
Restore script block logging and AMSI settings on WORKSTATION6
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated definitions
Review all processes on WORKSTATION6 around 2020-09-20 16:16 for additional indicators of compromise

title: Encoded PowerShell service creation disables security controls after network logon
summary: User pgustavo logged in from 172.18.39.5 and immediately created a new Windows service named 'Updater' that ran a PowerShell command with -enc flag. The decoded command disables ScriptBlockLogging, bypasses AMI antivirus, contacts http://10.10.10.5 to download and execute code, continuing the attack chain from ALERT-001.
evidence: pgustavo successful network logon from 172.18.39.5 at 16:16:58.212 on WORKSTATION6
Service 'Updater' installed by pgustavo at 16:16:58.214 running powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc with base64 encoding
Decoded PowerShell disables ScriptBlockLogging, bypasses AMI, downloads from http://10.10.10.5, runs downloaded code, contains nested base64
pgustavo is a domain user with normal host WORKSTATION5, unusual activity on WORKSTATION6
Connection to ALERT-001: same user executing same type of encoded PowerShell attack to disable security controls
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain from ALERT-001 - same user pgustavo from 172.18.39.5 now creating new service 'Updater' on WORKSTATION6 to run encoded PowerShell after the earlier attack disabled security controls

recommended_actions.action: Terminate 'Updater' service and kill spawned PowerShell processes
Reset credentials for pgustavo account and enforce MFA
Block http://10.10.10.5 and investigate as C2 infrastructure
Search other hosts for similarly named 'Updater' service creation
Review network logon from 172.18.39.5 for other suspicious activity
